scenes.narration: Can these dominoes cover the board? Remove two opposite corners. Sixty two squares remain, so the total area fits thirty one dominoes. But every domino covers two neighboring squares: one dark and one light. Watch what happens when we pair the colors. Keep every remaining square. Move each dark square beside one light square. We can make thirty pairs. And these two light squares are still waiting. There is no dark partner left. We rearranged the squares to count them, not to make a legal tiling. Any real tiling would also have to pair opposite colors. So none can exist. This is stronger than trying lots of arrangements. It rules out every arrangement. Matching area is not enough. Each piece also demands a matching pair.
